description: Version the Slack collaboration Skill so direct questions receive useful replies and recovery continues silently.

tasks.title: Publish the versioned Slack collaboration contract
tasks.description: Update the embedded `mohist-slack-collaboration` Markdown asset and Server catalog to version 1.1.0, preserving the existing v1 context shape and Server-owned reply anchor. Encode the ordered direct-question, useful-no-additional-information, valid-silence, explicit-reply, self-contained-result, audience-appropriate-mention, Web-timeline-progress, and silent-recovery rules in the asset, preserving all six rules and qualifiers from `docs/slack.md#slack-collaboration-rules-for-agents`, then extend Server contract and Slack ingress coverage to verify the published identity, hash, anchor, and root/follow-up behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The embedded asset at `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Services/Assets/mohist-slack-collaboration.skill.md` states that every direct human question receives a useful reply through the explicit Slack reply action, including a substantive no-additional-information answer rather than an acknowledgement-only message.

The asset preserves silence for a non-question turn with no conclusion, result, failure reason, or next step, while requiring self-contained conclusion/evidence/next-step replies for results and failures, delegator mentions for completed delegated work, mentions only when a person needs to act or notice the result, and fine-grained progress in the Web session timeline.

The asset instructs recovery after restart, Session recovery, or context compaction to reconstruct state from durable Session records and available Slack thread/startup context, preserve the existing Session and reply anchor, and avoid interruption or recovery narration; an outstanding direct question still takes precedence.

`SlackCollaborationSkillCatalog.Version` is `1.1.0`, and `Resolve()` continues to read the embedded resource and compute a lower-case SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 instruction bytes without a manually pinned hash or a context wire-version change.

Server contract tests assert the exact managed Skill name and version, derive and compare its hash, and use an explicit ordered six-entry checklist matching every bullet in `docs/slack.md#slack-collaboration-rules-for-agents`: speaker/useful conclusion or valid silence; no empty acknowledgements with the direct-question exception; delegated-result callback plus mention only when someone needs to act or notice the result; self-contained/proportionate replies with fine-grained progress in the Web session timeline; the Server-provided reply anchor; and silent resume from durable state and the thread. The checklist verifies every rule and qualifier without requiring one exact prose answer.

Server Slack ingress coverage continues to prove that a direct message uses its triggering message as the thread root, a threaded follow-up preserves the existing root and current triggering message, and both paths carry all Server-selected anchor fields without credentials or internal tokens.
The focused Server unit and Slack specification suites pass, including `SlackExecutionContextContractTests` and `SlackReplyAnchorIngressSpecs`.
No database migration, public API shape change, Agent definition change, credential-flow change, or Slack delivery/outbox behavior change is introduced by this slice.
tasks.output: Embedded `mohist-slack-collaboration` Skill v1.1.0, updated Server catalog contract tests, and passing Slack anchor ingress coverage.
tasks.notes: Keep `AgentSlackExecutionContext.CurrentVersion` at 1. The Server remains the asset authority; queued v1 contexts remain structurally compatible during rolling deployment and rollback.

tasks.title: Harden Runner Slack validation and envelope isolation
tasks.description: Make the Runner accept only a structurally valid v1 Slack context whose managed Skill name is exactly `mohist-slack-collaboration`, whose metadata is non-empty, and whose lower-case SHA-256 matches the delivered UTF-8 instructions. Exercise the shared AgentJob and follow-up injection path so valid Slack dispatches inline the updated Skill and anchor facts, malformed contexts fail before runtime invocation, and Web, CLI, and Workflow envelopes remain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: `readSlackExecutionContext` rejects unsupported context versions, incomplete reply anchors, incomplete Skill metadata, a Skill name other than `mohist-slack-collaboration`, and any content hash that does not exactly equal the lower-case SHA-256 digest of the supplied UTF-8 instructions.

A valid v1 context carrying the Server-published Skill name, version `1.1.0`, instructions, and matching hash resolves successfully and is inlined as the managed Slack Skill without pinning the content hash in Runner code.

AgentJob and follow-up dispatch tests prove malformed Slack contexts return the existing invalid/unavailable result before the Agent runtime is called, covering at least mismatched hash, wrong Skill name, and incomplete anchor or Skill metadata.

A valid Slack dispatch emits `[mohist-system-facts]` with the Server-provided reply anchor and includes the managed Skill instructions in the execution definition; the Runner does not add destination-selection behavior or expose the Skill body as system facts.

Normal execution envelopes remain unchanged and contain no Slack collaboration Skill, Slack reply anchor, or Slack system facts when no valid Slack provenance is present; the assertion covers the shared envelope path used by AgentJob and follow-up dispatches.

Runner type checks, test-boundary checks, and focused tests pass via `npm run typecheck:tests -w packages/runner`, `npm run check:test-boundaries -w packages/runner`, and `npm test -w packages/runner`.
The dependency graph remains scoped to Slack: no Web, CLI, or Workflow execution receives Slack-specific instructions or facts as a side effect.
tasks.output: Exact managed-Skill validation in the Runner, pre-runtime rejection tests, Slack envelope injection coverage, and non-Slack envelope regression coverage.
tasks.notes: Reuse `readSlackExecutionContext`, `inlineSlackCollaborationSkill`, `buildExecutionEnvelope`, `agent-job-executor`, and `followup-handler`. Do not add a question classifier, recovery marker, Server fallback reply, or new context fields.
